pythagoras.subject:
Explain Pythagoras' theorem using an animated right-angled triangle.
Show the sides a, b and hypotenuse c.
Clearly display a² + b² = c².
Explain that the hypotenuse is the longest side.
pythagoras.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="100%" height="100%">
    <title>Pythagoras Theorem Animated Explanation</title>
    
    <defs>
        <style>
            .bg { fill: #f8fafc; }
            .title { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: bold; fill: #1e293b; text-anchor: middle; }
            .subtitle { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; fill: #475569; text-anchor: middle; }
            .label { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; font-weight: bold; fill: #1e293b; text-anchor: middle; dominant-baseline: middle; }
            .formula { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 28px; font-weight: bold; fill: #0f172a; text-anchor: middle; }
            .triangle { fill: #ffffff; stroke: #0ea5e9; stroke-width: 4; stroke-linejoin: round; }
            .sq-a { fill: #fca5a5; fill-opacity: 0.8; stroke: #ef4444; stroke-width: 3; }
            .sq-b { fill: #93c5fd; fill-opacity: 0.8; stroke: #3b82f6; stroke-width: 3; }
            .sq-c { fill: #86efac; fill-opacity: 0.8; stroke: #22c55e; stroke-width: 3; }
            .grid { stroke: #e2e8f0; stroke-width: 1; }
            
            @keyframes pulse-c {
                0% { fill-opacity: 0.6; stroke-width: 3; }
                50% { fill-opacity: 0.9; stroke-width: 5; }
                100% { fill-opacity: 0.6; stroke-width: 3; }
            }
            .sq-c-anim {
                animation: pulse-c 4s infinite ease-in-out;
            }
        </style>
        
        <!-- Grid pattern for area squares -->
        <pattern id="grid-a" width="30" height="30" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
            <path d="M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30" fill="none" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.3"/>
        </pattern>
        <pattern id="grid-b" width="30" height="30" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
            <path d="M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30" fill="none" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.3"/>
        </pattern>
        <pattern id="grid-c" width="30" height="30" patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
            <path d="M 30 0 L 0 0 0 30" fill="none" stroke="#22c55e" stroke-width="0.5" stroke-opacity="0.3"/>
        </pattern>
    </defs>

    <!-- Background -->
    <rect width="800" height="500" class="bg" />

    <!-- Title and Subtitle -->
    <text x="400" y="40" class="title">Pythagoras' Theorem</text>
    <text x="400" y="70" class="subtitle">For a right-angled triangle: a² + b² = c²</text>

    <!-- Background Grid lines for visual aid -->
    <path d="M 50 120 L 750 120 M 50 180 L 750 180 M 50 240 L 750 240 M 50 300 L 750 300 M 50 360 L 750 360 M 50 420 L 750 420" class="grid" />

    <!-- 
      Triangle coordinates:
      A = (250, 310)
      B = (250, 190) -> vertical height = 120 (4 units * 30px)
      C = (410, 310) -> horizontal base = 160 (5.33 units... wait let's use exact 3-4-5 scale)
      Let scale be 30px per unit.
      Side a (vertical) = 3 units = 90px. From y=220 to y=310 at x=220.
      Side b (horizontal) = 4 units = 120px. From x=220 to x=340 at y=310.
      Side c (hypotenuse) = 5 units = 150px. From (220, 220) to (340, 310).
      
      Let's place the main triangle at:
      Vertex Right Angle: (250, 340)
      Vertex Top: (250, 220)   [Height = 120px = 4 units]
      Vertex Right: (410, 340) [Base = 160px = 5 units? Let's use 3-4-5: height=90, base=120, hyp=150]
    -->

    <!-- 
      RE-CALCULATING for 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 30:
      Right Angle at (260, 340)
      Top vertex (Side a vertical): (260, 220) -> length 120 (4 units)
      Right vertex (Side b horizontal): (420, 340) -> length 160 (3 units? Let's do base=120, height=160)
      
      Let:
      Right Angle (RA) = (280, 360)
      Top (T) = (280, 240) [Vertical side a = 120px]
      Right (R) = (440, 360) [Horizontal side b = 160px]
      Hypotenuse connects (280, 240) and (440, 360). Length = sqrt(120^2 + 160^2) = 200px (5 units of 40px).
    -->

    <!-- Square on Side a (Left, 120x120, projecting left from x=160 to 280, y=240 to 360) -->
    <rect x="160" y="240" width="120" height="120" class="sq-a" />
    <rect x="160" y="240" width="120" height="120" fill="url(#grid-a)" />
    
    <!-- Square on Side b (Bottom, 160x160, projecting down from y=360 to 520 - wait, max is 500, let's adjust upward!) -->

    <!--
      NEW POSITIONING TO FIT 800x500 cleanly:
      Right Angle (RA) = (260, 300)
      Top Vertex (T) = (260, 180) -> Side a = 120px (3 units of 40px)
      Right Vertex (R) = (420, 300) -> Side b = 160px (4 units of 40px)
      Hypotenuse = 200px (5 units of 40px) from (260, 180) to (420, 300)
    -->

    <!-- Square on Side a (Left): x = 260 - 120 = 140. y = 180 to 300. Width=120, Height=120 -->
    <rect x="140" y="180" width="120" height="120" class="sq-a" />
    <rect x="140" y="180" width="120" height="120" fill="url(#grid-a)" />

    <!-- Square on Side b (Bottom): x = 260 to 420. y = 300 to 300+160 = 460. Width=160, Height=160 -->
    <rect x="260" y="300" width="160" height="160" class="sq-b" />
    <rect x="260" y="300" width="160" height="160" fill="url(#grid-b)" />

    <!-- 
      Square on Hypotenuse (c):
      Hypotenuse vector is from (260, 180) to (420, 300).
      dx = 160, dy = 120.
      Perpendicular outward vector (to the top-left/up-right): (-dy, dx) = (-120, 160).
      The square builds outward from the hypotenuse.
      Corners of hypotenuse: P1(260, 180) and P2(420, 300).
      Outward square points: 
      P1 -> P1 + (-120, 160) = (140, 340) ... wait, that goes into the triangle.
      Other side: P1 + (120, -160) = (380, 20)
      P2 + (120, -160) = (540, 140)
      Let's verify polygon points for square c:
      (260, 180) -> (420, 300) -> (540, 140) -> (380, 20) -> cycle.
    -->
    <polygon points="260,180 420,300 540,140 380,20" class="sq-c sq-c-anim" />
    <polygon points="260,180 420,300 540,140 380,20" fill="url(#grid-c)" />

    <!-- The Triangle itself (drawn over the squares so edges are crisp) -->
    <polygon points="260,180 260,300 420,300" class="triangle" />

    <!-- Right angle indicator -->
    <polyline points="260,280 280,280 280,300" fill="none" stroke="#0ea5e9" stroke-width="3" />

    <!-- Labels for Sides -->
    <text x="200" y="235" class="label" fill="#b91c1c">a = 3</text>
    <text x="340" y="335" class="label" fill="#1d4ed8">b = 4</text>
    <text x="475" y="210" class="label" fill="#15803d">c = 5</text>

    <!-- Labels for Areas inside squares -->
    <text x="200" y="240" class="label" fill="#991b1b" font-size="16">a² = 9</text>
    <text x="340" y="375" class="label" fill="#1e40af" font-size="16">b² = 16</text>
    <text x="460" y="220" class="label" fill="#166534" font-size="16">c² = 25</text>

    <!-- Side labels outside triangle -->
    <text x="120" y="245" class="subtitle" font-weight="bold" fill="#ef4444">Side a</text>
    <text x="340" y="480" class="subtitle" font-weight="bold" fill="#3b82f6">Side b (Base)</text>
    <text x="610" y="80" class="subtitle" font-weight="bold" fill="#22c55e">Hypotenuse (c)</text>

    <!-- Mathematical breakdown box on the right -->
    <rect x="580" y="140" width="190" height="300" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="2" />
    
    <text x="675" y="180" class="label" font-size="18">Area Calculation</text>
    
    <text x="675" y="230" class="formula" font-size="22" fill="#ef4444">a² = 3² = 9</text>
    <text x="675" y="280" class="formula" font-size="22" fill="#3b82f6">b² = 4² = 16</text>
    
    <line x1="605" y1="310" x2="745" y2="310" stroke="#94a3b8" stroke-width="2" />
    
    <text x="675" y="350" class="formula" font-size="22" fill="#22c55e">a² + b² = c²</text>
    <text x="675" y="390" class="formula" font-size="20" fill="#0f172a">9 + 16 = 25</text>
    <text x="675" y="425" class="formula" font-size="18" fill="#15803d">c = √25 = 5</text>

    <!-- Connecting explanatory arrows/lines -->
    <line x1="380" y1="20" x2="570" y2="120" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4" />
</svg>

circle.subject:
Create an educational animated diagram of a circle.
Clearly label centre, radius, diameter, chord and circumference.
Show that the diameter passes through the centre
and is twice the radius.
circle.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="800" height="500">
  <title>Circle Theorems and Parts of a Circle</title>
  
  <style>
    .title { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 22px; font-weight: bold; fill: #1e293b; text-anchor: middle; }
    .label { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: bold; fill: #334155; }
    .formula { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: bold; fill: #0f172a; text-anchor: middle; }
    .subtext { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; fill: #475569; text-anchor: middle; }
    
    .bg { fill: #f8fafc; stroke: #cbd5e1; stroke-width: 2; rx: 12; }
    .circle-boundary { fill: #ffffff; stroke: #2563eb; stroke-width: 4; }
    
    .line-radius { stroke: #16a34a; stroke-width: 3.5; stroke-dasharray: 6,4; }
    .line-diameter-left { stroke: #dc2626; stroke-width: 4; }
    .line-diameter-right { stroke: #2563eb; stroke-width: 4; }
    .line-chord { stroke: #9333ea; stroke-width: 3.5; }
    
    .leader { stroke: #64748b; stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; }
    .point { fill: #0f172a; }
    .center-point { fill: #dc2626; }
    
    .anim-radius {
      animation: pulseRadius 3s infinite ease-in-out;
    }
    
    @keyframes pulseRadius {
      0% { opacity: 0.4; stroke-width: 3; }
      50% { opacity: 1; stroke-width: 5; }
      100% { opacity: 0.4; stroke-width: 3; }
    }
  </style>

  <!-- Background Card -->
  <rect x="15" y="15" width="770" height="470" class="bg" />

  <!-- Title -->
  <text x="400" y="45" class="title">Parts of a Circle & Key Properties</text>

  <!-- Circle definition: Center at (380, 230), Radius = 120 -->
  
  <!-- Circumference Area -->
  <circle cx="380" cy="230" r="120" class="circle-boundary" />

  <!-- Chord (Endpoints: x=280, y=130 to x=480, y=130 - clearly not through center 380,230) -->
  <line x1="280" y1="135" x2="480" y2="135" class="line-chord" />
  
  <!-- Diameter Left Half (Red) - passes through center (380, 230) to left edge (260, 230) -->
  <line x1="260" y1="230" x2="380" y2="230" class="line-diameter-left" />

  <!-- Diameter Right Half (Blue) - passes through center (380, 230) to right edge (500, 230) -->
  <line x1="380" y1="230" x2="500" y2="230" class="line-diameter-right" />

  <!-- Radius (Green, animated) - from center (380, 230) to top-right edge (465, 145) -->
  <line x1="380" y1="230" x2="465" y2="145" class="line-radius anim-radius" />

  <!-- Points -->
  <circle cx="380" cy="230" r="5" class="center-point" />
  <circle cx="465" cy="145" r="4" class="point" />
  <circle cx="280" cy="135" r="4" class="point" />
  <circle cx="480" cy="135" r="4" class="point" />
  <circle cx="500" cy="230" r="4" class="point" />

  <!-- Leader Lines and Labels -->
  
  <!-- Center Label -->
  <polyline points="380,230 330,280 300,280" class="leader" />
  <circle cx="380" cy="230" r="2" class="point" />
  <text x="290" y="284" class="label" text-anchor="end">Centre</text>

  <!-- Radius Label -->
  <polyline points="422,187 450,110 490,110" class="leader" />
  <text x="500" y="114" class="label">Radius ($r$)</text>

  <!-- Diameter Label (Pointing to the full diameter line) -->
  <polyline points="440,230 460,330 490,330" class="leader" />
  <text x="500" y="334" class="label">Diameter ($d$)</text>

  <!-- Chord Label -->
  <polyline points="380,135 340,90 290,90" class="leader" />
  <text x="280" y="94" class="label" text-anchor="end">Chord</text>

  <!-- Circumference Label -->
  <polyline points="260,180 200,180 160,180" class="leader" />
  <text x="150" y="184" class="label" text-anchor="end">Circumference</text>

  <!-- Mathematical Relationship Panel / Box -->
  <rect x="530" y="80" width="235" height="180" rx="8" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#cbd5e1" stroke-width="1.5" />
  <text x="647" y="110" class="formula">Key Mathematical Rules</text>
  
  <line x1="550" y1="125" x2="745" y2="125" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="1" />

  <text x="647" y="150" class="formula" fill="#dc2626">Diameter = 2 × Radius</text>
  <text x="647" y="175" class="subtext">Passes through the centre</text>

  <text x="647" y="215" class="formula" fill="#16a34a">Radius = Diameter ÷ 2</text>
  <text x="647" y="240" class="subtext">Half the length of the diameter</text>

  <!-- Bottom Educational Note -->
  <rect x="55" y="415" width="690" height="45" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#bfdbfe" stroke-width="1" />
  <text x="400" y="442" class="subtext" font-size="14" fill="#1e40af">
    Note: A chord is a straight line joining two points on the circumference. The diameter is the longest chord.
  </text>

</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="800" height="500">
  <title>Series Circuit: Current and Voltage</title>
  
  <style>
    .bg { fill: #f8fafc; }
    .panel { fill: #ffffff; stroke: #cbd5e1; stroke-width: 2; rx: 12; }
    .title-text { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 20px; font-weight: bold; fill: #1e293b; text-anchor: middle; }
    .label { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: bold; fill: #334155; }
    .sublabel { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; fill: #64748b; }
    .wire { fill: none; stroke: #475569; stroke-width: 4; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }
    .electron { fill: #f59e0b; }
    .bullet { font-size: 13px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; fill: #334155; }
    
    @keyframes flow {
      from { stroke-dashoffset: 24; }
      to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; }
    }
    
    .current-flow {
      stroke: #f59e0b;
      stroke-width: 4;
      stroke-linecap: round;
      stroke-dasharray: 6 12;
      animation: flow 1s linear infinite;
    }
  </style>

  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="800" height="500" class="bg" />

  <!-- Main Title -->
  <text x="400" y="35" class="title-text">Series Circuit: Current & Voltage</text>

  <!-- Circuit Diagram Panel -->
  <rect x="40" y="60" width="460" height="400" class="panel" />

  <!-- The Circuit Wires (Base) -->
  <path d="M 120 250 L 120 140 L 420 140 L 420 360 L 120 360 L 120 280" class="wire" />

  <!-- Animated Current Path -->
  <path d="M 120 250 L 120 140 L 420 140 L 420 360 L 120 360 L 120 280" class="current-flow" />

  <!-- Cell / Power Supply (Left) -->
  <!-- Long line (positive) -->
  <line x1="105" y1="230" x2="135" y2="230" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" />
  <!-- Short line (negative) -->
  <line x1="112" y1="240" x2="128" y2="240" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" />
  <!-- Long line (positive) -->
  <line x1="105" y1="250" x2="135" y2="250" stroke="#ef4444" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" />
  <!-- Short line (negative) -->
  <line x1="112" y1="260" x2="128" y2="260" stroke="#3b82f6" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" />
  
  <text x="75" y="250" class="label" text-anchor="end">Cell</text>
  <text x="75" y="268" class="sublabel" text-anchor="end">6 V</text>

  <!-- Resistor 1 / Lamp 1 (Top) -->
  <rect x="230" y="125" width="60" height="30" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="3" rx="4" />
  <text x="260" y="110" class="label" text-anchor="middle">Lamp 1</text>
  <text x="260" y="178" class="sublabel" text-anchor="middle">V₁ = 3 V</text>

  <!-- Resistor 2 / Lamp 2 (Right) -->
  <rect x="405" y="220" width="30" height="60" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="3" rx="4" />
  <text x="465" y="245" class="label" text-anchor="start">Lamp 2</text>
  <text x="465" y="263" class="sublabel" text-anchor="start">V₂ = 3 V</text>

  <!-- Ammeter (Bottom) -->
  <circle cx="260" cy="360" r="18" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f172a" stroke-width="3" />
  <text x="260" y="365" class="label" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16">A</text>
  <text x="260" y="398" class="sublabel" text-anchor="middle">Current = 0.5 A</text>

  <!-- Circuit Rules Explanation Panel -->
  <rect x="520" y="60" width="240" height="400" class="panel" />
  
  <text x="640" y="95" class="label" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#1e293b">Key Rules</text>

  <!-- Rule 1 -->
  <circle cx="545" cy="135" r="4" fill="#3b82f6" />
  <text x="560" y="140" class="bullet" font-weight="bold">Single Loop:</text>
  <text x="560" y="160" class="bullet">There is only one path</text>
  <text x="560" y="178" class="bullet">for charge to flow.</text>

  <!-- Rule 2 -->
  <circle cx="545" cy="225" r="4" fill="#3b82f6" />
  <text x="560" y="230" class="bullet" font-weight="bold">Current is Same:</text>
  <text x="560" y="250" class="bullet">The current is identical</text>
  <text x="560" y="268" class="bullet">at all points in the loop.</text>

  <!-- Rule 3 -->
  <circle cx="545" cy="315" r="4" fill="#3b82f6" />
  <text x="560" y="320" class="bullet" font-weight="bold">Voltage is Shared:</text>
  <text x="560" y="340" class="bullet">Cell voltage (6V) is</text>
  <text x="560" y="358" class="bullet">shared between the</text>
  <text x="560" y="376" class="bullet">components (3V + 3V).</text>

  <!-- Interactive/Educational Legend Footer inside panel -->
  <line x1="540" y1="410" x2="740" y2="410" stroke="#e2e8f0" stroke-width="2" />
  <circle cx="555" cy="433" r="6" class="electron" />
  <text x="575" y="437" class="sublabel">Electron Flow</text>

</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="800" height="500">
    <title>Photosynthesis GCSE Science Diagram</title>

    <defs>
        <style>
            .bg { fill: #f0f7f4; }
            .soil { fill: #8d5524; }
            .sun-core { fill: #ffcc00; }
            .leaf { fill: #2e8b57; stroke: #1e5631; stroke-width: 4; }
            .stem { fill: #4a7c59; stroke: #2d4f37; stroke-width: 3; }

    <!-- Floating Bubble Elements for visual flair -->
    <circle cx="530" cy="300" r="4" fill="#2ecc71" opacity="0.6">

        <animate attributeName="opacity" values="0;1;0" dur="2.5s" repeatCount="indefinite" />
    </circle>

</svg>

states_of_matter.subject:
Create an animated educational diagram comparing solid,
liquid and gas particle arrangements.
Show solid particles closely packed and vibrating in place.
Show liquid particles close together but moving past each other.
Show gas particles far apart and moving quickly.
